title: Audit ingest compactification & write-amplification mitigation
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background:
Redwood's audit pipeline has grown write amplification and index fragmentation during peak tenant churn and bursty admin activity. This causes increased GPU/IO load in Dedicated clusters and higher storage egress/coldstore costs in Private deployments. Current hotspots are: small frequent writes for RBAC events, SSO/SAML handshakes, and admin changes; index churn from late-arriving enrichment; and whole-shard rewrites during TTL compaction windows.

Goal:
Reduce end-to-end write amplification and index rewrite volume by at least 40% for audit events while preserving query latency for recent hotpath queries (<= 200ms P95 for admin/forensic queries) and maintain full-fidelity retention for regulated tenants. Keep changes transparent to Console and downstream compliance exports.

Scope / Non-goals:
- In scope: ingestion-side queuing, per-tenant shard-slicing, differential compaction, compaction scheduling heuristics, enriched-event deduplication, metrics and dashboards, canary rollout plan.
- Out of scope: long-term immutable archival format redesign, downstream analytics reindexing (follow-up project).

Proposed approach (high level):
1) Compactification layer: introduce a mid-stream compaction step that coalesces frequent small audit events into a compacted delta representation for the immediate hot window (configurable by tenant). This reduces write amplification by avoiding repeated full-index writes for every small event.
2) Differential compaction: perform in-shard delta compaction instead of whole-shard rewrites. Track a lightweight compaction bitmap per shard to identify ranges needing rewrite.
3) Shard-slicing and write routing: slice hot shards by tenant/activity window so that high-churn tenants are isolated and compacted more aggressively. Use write routing to place slices on nodes with spare IO capacity.
4) Adaptive TTL windows: shift TTL-triggered compaction to staggered windows using probabilistic staggering to avoid compaction storms; allow escape hatch to force immediate resume for compliance-critical deletes.
5) Enrichment dedup cache: short-lived KV cache at the enrichment step keyed by event fingerprint to deduplicate redundant enrichment writes produced by retries.
6) Cost control knobs: per-tenant write-rate quotas and a soft-throttle that prefers compactified writes when nearing cost thresholds. Expose estimates in Console cost preview.

Implementation details / acceptance criteria:
- Implement compactification as an optional middleware in the ingest pipeline behind a feature flag. Must be toggleable per-tenant.
- Differential compaction must support incremental index-rewrite segments and expose metrics: bytes_rewritten, rewrite_ops, compaction_latency_ms.
- Add per-slice routing policy that can be set by autoscaler to avoid overloading disk IO.
- Bench target: end-to-end write amplification (bytes_written/bytes_ingested) reduced >= 40% on synthetic churn workload (workload spec attached).
- Query latency: admin/forensic queries on last 7 days must remain <= 200ms P95 in canary cluster.
- Storage: reduce coldstore spillover by 20% in simulated retention mix (30/365/1095).

Rollout plan:
- Phase A: Implement compactification and dedupe cache behind feature flag; unit + integration tests; perf harness to measure write amplification. (Canary customers: internal infra+security orgs)
- Phase B: Enable shard-slicing and differential compaction in canary cluster; run 72h stress test and capacity analysis.
- Phase C: Gradual rollout to a subset of high-churn tenants with cost preview in Console and opt-out.
- Phase D: Full rollout and deprecate legacy full-shard TTL compaction in favor of staggered differential compaction.

Monitoring & dashboards:
- New dashboard: Audit Compactification Health (panels: bytes_ingested, bytes_written, write_amplification_ratio, compaction_ops/s, compaction_backlog, per-tenant rewrite_bytes).
- Alerts: compaction_backlog > 30 minutes for >5% of hot shards; write_amplification_ratio increase >10% month-over-month; compaction_error_rate > 0.5%.

Security & compliance considerations:
- Compaction must preserve a verifiable event stream for regulatory audits. We will attach a compaction manifest to compacted segments that lists event fingerprints and offsets so auditors can reconstruct originals if needed.
- Feature flag and per-tenant opt-out to allow tenants with strict audit immutability requirements to bypass compactification.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for compaction logic and dedupe cache semantics.
- Integration tests with enrichment pipeline ensuring late-arrival enrichment merges into compacted deltas.
- Load tests using workload generator (script in infra/perf/audit-churn) with target QPS and churn mix; compare bytes_written baseline vs. compactified.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Manifest size vs. cost: attaching full manifests increases metadata storage. We propose a fingerprint manifest with chunked lookups to bound metadata growth.
- Latency vs. compaction aggressiveness: more aggressive compaction reduces writes but can add tail latency on the write path. We'll tune via canary.

Next steps / immediate tasks:
- Spike: implement compactification prototype in ingest worker (owner: Miguel). Duration 1 week.
- Define workload spec for perf team (owner: Priya Menon).
- Draft Console UX for opt-out + cost preview (owner: Lina Gomez, design).
acceptance_criteria: Feature flag per-tenant to enable compactification
Write amplification reduced by >= 40% on synthetic churn test
Compaction manifest created for each compacted segment
Monitoring dashboard and alerts in place
comments: 2026-03-02 Miguel Torres: Spike started. Built prototype that coalesces events into a delta blob and writes a compact record to the index. Initial microbench shows 2.3x reduction on toy workload.
2026-03-04 Priya Menon (PM): Confirmed scope and prioritized canary tenants (security-team-internal, payments-prod). Added cost preview requirement for Console.
2026-03-06 Ethan Li (Security): Requested compaction manifest format to include cryptographic fingerprinting to support audit reconstruction. Suggest using SHA256 of canonical event JSON.
2026-03-08 Lina Gomez (Design): UX draft for opt-out modal and per-tenant compactification toggle posted to Confluence. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Audit+Compactification

2026-03-10 Miguel Torres: Integration test failing for late-enrichment merging; found race where enrichment retry writes happen after compactification commit. Proposed solution: enrichment layer writes to staging KV with idempotency token; compactifier consumes staging. Will implement next iteration.
2026-03-11 QA: Added performance harness run scheduled for 2026-03-15. Goal: 72h run with traffic profile 'churn-heavy-50k'
